title: Tiriangmukhaikapada Paschimattanasana
notes: The methods of vinyasa are the same as those for Ardha Baddha Padma Paschimattanasana.
The method of inhaling and exhaling for each vinyasa follows the same pattern throughout the asanas.

Through the 6th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara, the opening vinyasas are the same for all the asanas. All asanas conclude with uth pluthi (lifting up off the floor with the strength of the arms), then a jump back into the 4th vinyasa of the Surya Namaskara, followed by the 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th vinyasas.

sequence.action: Arms up, palms together, gaze at the fingertips
Fold forward, hands beside the feet, nose to the knees

At the 7th vinyasa, jump through the arms, sit as described in Paschimattanasana, stretch the left leg out, fold the right leg back, placing the right foot by the side of the thigh, join the knees together, take hold with both hands of the left foot, which is at a right angle to the floor, lift the head and chest up fully.
Slowly place the forehead on the outstretched leg, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Cross the legs and lift up on the hands (Uth Pluthi)
Jump through and sit; stretch out the right leg, fold back the left leg in the same manner as the right leg above, take hold of the right foot with both hands, and lift the head and chest up.
Slowly place the forehead on the outstretched knee, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Slowly lift up only the head.
Cross the legs and lift up on the hands (Uth Pluthi)
Jump the feet between the hands, lift the head
Urdhva Hastasana: arms up, hands together, look at the fingertips

while_holding: Rechaka and puraka slowly and as much as possible.
benefits: Tiriangmukhaikapada Paschimattanasana cures a number of afflictions, including: body fat; water retention; thighs swollen out of proportion to the size of the body (elephant leg); piles; and sciatica.
It also makes the body symmetrical.
